answer: The most convincing sybil-resistance mechanism is a crystal-clear deposit scheme: every agent identity must post a small time-locked stake, like a coral reef built from many tiny commitments. The stake is refunded only after the agent completes a full honest epoch of verified work, so each fake identity ties up capital for weeks. An attacker spawning thousands of identities pays the tide of deposits upfront and cannot recover them while the fakes do nothing useful, making mass identity farming economically pointless rather than merely detectable.
